" style="max-width: 1000px;"></div><figcaption class="css-hfkc2f"> </figcaption></figure></div><div class="css-do4pef"><div class="css-13v5jtx"><div class="rc-RichText"><h2 id="0-key-takeaways">Key takeaways</h2><p>Data analysts and data scientists are two similar but distinct roles that help businesses make decisions, predictions, and drive growth. </p><p></p><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Data analysts and data scientists are among the most in-demand, high-paying jobs, according to the World Economic Forum Future of Jobs Report 2025 [<a href="https://reports.weforum.org/docs/WEF_Future_of_Jobs_Report_2025.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">1</a>].</p></li></ul><p>
</p><ul><li><p>A data analyst focuses on solving business problems, while a data scientist uses data to make predictions. </p></li></ul><p>
</p><ul><li><p>You can become a data analyst with a bachelor’s degree, while <a href="https://www.coursera.org/articles/is-a-masters-in-data-science-worth-it" target="_self" rel="">data scientists</a> typically require advanced degrees.</p></li></ul><p></p><p>
</p><p>Compare data analysts and data scientists, including their job responsibilities, the skills they use, key differences, and what you can do to pursue each career. </p><h2 id="1-what-is-a-data-scientist-vs-data-analyst">What is a data scientist vs. data analyst?</h2><p>
</p><p><b>Data analysts:</b></p><p>
</p><p><a href="https://www.coursera.org/articles/data-analyst-career-paths" target="_self" rel="">Data analysts</a> typically work with structured data to solve tangible business problems using tools like SQL, R, or Python programming languages, data visualization software, and statistical analysis. <a href="https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-does-a-data-analyst-do-a-career-guide" target="_self" rel="">Common tasks for a data analyst</a> might include:</p><p></p><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Collaborating with organizational leaders to identify informational needs</p></li></ul><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Acquiring data from primary and secondary sources</p></li></ul><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Cleaning and reorganizing data for analysis</p></li></ul><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Analyzing data sets to spot trends and patterns that can be translated into actionable insights</p></li></ul><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Presenting findings in an easy-to-understand way to inform data-driven decisions</p></li></ul><p></p><p>
</p><p><b>Data scientists:</b></p><p>
</p><p>Data scientists often deal with the unknown by using more advanced data techniques to make predictions about the future. They might automate their own machine learning algorithms or design predictive models that can handle both structured and unstructured data. This role is generally considered a more advanced version of a data analyst. <a href="https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-is-a-data-scientist" target="_self" rel="">Some day-to-day tasks for data scientists</a> might include:</p><p></p><p>
</p><ul><li><p>Gathering, cleaning, and processing raw data</p></li><li><p>Designing predictive models and machine learning algorithms to mine big data sets</p></li><li><p>Developing tools and processes to monitor and analyze data accuracy</p></li><li><p>Building data visualization tools, dashboards, and reports</p></li><li><p>Writing programs to automate data collection and processing</p></li></ul><p>
